changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For payments leaders: 'See the approvals you're losing, market by market, in your own data. We'll show you yours by country, card type and issuer, with the reasons and the money left on the table.' Use 'approvals', not 'authorization'. Keep the average uplift figure only as supporting proof under the customer's own numbers. Never make it the headline. Package the result as a one-page summary of their markets, their approvals and the revenue at stake, so a payments lead can forward it to the CFO.
changes.why: We answered with the average-uplift deck and the buyer rejected it with 'that's an average. What's mine?' He also said 'I can't take an average to my CFO', who approved the decision, and he speaks of 'approvals' and 'Money left on the table' rather than authorization and uplift.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For accounts with a payments leader: lead with a named person who looks at your approval numbers every month, with a monthly market-by-market approvals review. Keep response-time tiers as secondary detail.
changes.why: The buyer asked 'who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month', the rep had no name to give, and what he valued was 'A market-by-market view of their own approval rates, with reasons', not ticket response times.

changes.change: Answer to 'local acquiring' / 'Local cards, local rails': offer a per-market analysis of the customer's own traffic by country, card type and issuer, with reasons and fixable findings, delivered fast enough to sit beside a competitor's test. Add a per-market statement of how we handle local cards only after product confirms what we can truthfully claim.
changes.why: Adyen set the terms with a test on the buyer's own traffic, broken down 'by country, on this card type, by issuer. And why.' Our own analysis produced 'Real findings. Things we could have fixed.', but it 'landed three weeks after he asked, and by then the test was finished.'

changes.change: 'New payments leader' play for account teams: when the original buyer of a payments account leaves, find the replacement. Open with their own declines by country and a standing approvals review before they ask, instead of the developer-led story.
changes.why: The original buyer left and a new head of payments first 'pull[ed] declines by country'. The rep 'didn't know they'd hired a head of payments', so nobody re-sold the account to him on the criteria he measured.
